source_name: skopjehacklab/e-nabavki — open-source machine-friendly scraper/dataset for e-nabavki.gov.mk
why_relevant: Civic-tech project that documents ESJN's undocumented endpoints and dossier URL patterns and produces machine-readable extracts. It is the fastest way to learn the portal's internal API surface (bypassing the 403/ASP.NET friction) and to validate a collection design.

source_name: Е-Пазар (state electronic marketplace for low-value procurement)
why_relevant: Companion platform to ESJN for small-value purchases; captures the long tail of state IT/hardware buying (card readers, terminals, small software licences) that never reaches the notice threshold but still indicates institutional adoption.

source_name: Државен завод за ревизија (State Audit Office) — audit reports on contracting authorities
why_relevant: Audits of the Ministry of Finance, funds, and procurement bodies routinely describe IT/payment-system contracts, their value, delays and non-compliance findings — a retrospective, high-credibility check on what was actually delivered versus what the notice promised, and a discovery route to contracts poorly represented on ESJN.

source_name: Агенција за заштита на правото на слободен пристап до информации од јавен карактер (ASPI) / slobodenpristap.mk — FOI route to procurement bodies
why_relevant: Maintains the register of information holders (иматели на информации) with FOI officers per institution, and slobodenpristap.mk hosts public FOI requests/answers. This is the legal fallback for obtaining tender documentation, contract annexes or specifications that are not published — and the register itself is a complete actor map of contracting authorities.

source_name: Uslugi.gov.mk — national institution/services register
why_relevant: Authoritative directory of state institutions and the services they run (including NBRSM and UJP entries). Useful for building and normalising the contracting-authority actor map that the ESJN and TED collectors filter on, and for spotting new/renamed bodies.

source_name: US Commercial Service Country Commercial Guide — North Macedonia: Selling to the Public Sector / Trade Financing
why_relevant: Concise, regularly updated English orientation to the MK public procurement market (~€1bn/yr, EPPS centralisation, which IFIs fund what). Useful as a stable context/pointer document for onboarding new analysts and for confirming which donor channels matter — not a tender feed.

source_name: ASEE / Asseco SEE — News & Events (regional press releases incl. North Macedonia)
why_relevant: ASEE is one of the few vendors that publicly names MK bank customers (e.g. 'New ATMs for Komercijalna Bank', 'ASEE in Macedonia Completed Most Complex Banks' Merger in SEE Region') and states it has completed 120+ Basel/IAS/IFRS 9 compliance implementations across markets including North Macedonia. Its press stream is the closest public trace of which MK private bank is implementing which regulatory/compliance mandate and on what timeline.

source_name: Netcetera — References / customer stories (Skopje delivery centre, MK bank clients)
why_relevant: Netcetera publishes named bank references including Halkbank (North Macedonia) digital wallet / contactless payments, and is a 3-D Secure market leader — directly relevant to SCA/PSD2-style mandates that MK banks must meet. Its reference and news pages reveal which MK bank bought which payment-security component and when it went live.

source_name: CaSys International (International Card System AD Skopje) — services & client list
why_relevant: Independent card processor serving essentially the whole MK private-bank sector (NLB, Stopanska, Sparkasse, Komercijalna, ProCredit, TTK, Uni, Ziraat, Halk etc.). Because it is the shared processing layer, any card-scheme or regulatory mandate (EMV, 3DS/SCA, tokenisation, instant card payments) shows up first in CaSys' service and news pages — a single pointer to many banks' compliance timelines.

source_name: KIBS AD Skopje — Clearing house news & resources (instant payments / SEPA readiness)
why_relevant: KIBS operates MK's clearing and the domestic instant-payments scheme and publishes PDFs on EU-regulation readiness (Instant Payments Regulation, SEPA). Its notices state which banks have started integration and when production go-live/licensing from NBRM occurs — i.e. private-bank compliance deadlines that never appear in a public tender.

source_name: Nextsense (Skopje) — digital identity / e-signature vendor, incl. OneID with KIBS
why_relevant: Local vendor of e-identity/e-signature and document solutions to finance and government; co-launched OneID, the first Macedonian electronic identification service, with KIBS. eIDAS-aligned trust services are a compliance mandate for banks (remote onboarding, qualified e-signature), so Nextsense's customer and news pages are an indirect trace of which MK banks are implementing eID/eSign and when.

source_name: Evrotrust Technologies DOOEL Skopje — qualified trust service provider (MK)
why_relevant: Registered MK electronic identification scheme provider under the national law transposing eIDAS. Its compliance/legal pages and partner references indicate which financial institutions rely on qualified e-signature/remote identification, a live regulatory mandate for onboarding and AML KYC.

source_name: Printec Group — North Macedonia country page & solutions/resources
why_relevant: Present in MK since 2006 as a technology partner to leading financial institutions; publishes solution pages, blog and resources on ATM/POS, cash handling and CEE EFT-POS landscape. Useful as a supplier-ecosystem trace of self-service and cash-automation projects at private MK banks.

source_name: MASIT — Chamber of ICT Companies of North Macedonia, member directory
why_relevant: Authoritative local directory of ICT vendors; already surfaced CaSys and KIBS profiles. Best single snowball device for enumerating the MK supplier ecosystem (core banking, processing, integration, security) whose sites then reveal bank customers.

source_name: Bankarstvo.mk — MK banking trade news
why_relevant: Local specialist banking outlet that carries bank-side announcements of new systems and go-lives (new mBanka at Komercijalna, new e-banking portal, Komercijalna joining SEPA, e-Faktura presented to the banking sector, SCA from 1 March 2026). Articles frequently name the mandate and the date even when they do not name the vendor — an entry point to then find the supplier press release.

source_name: Semos (Skopje) — custom business solutions incl. mobile banking
why_relevant: Long-established MK system integrator that explicitly markets mobile-banking software; a candidate supplier behind unattributed bank app launches. Its solution/case pages are an indirect trace of which private bank refreshed a channel and when.

source_name: IWConnect — finance & banking solutions, MK engineering house
why_relevant: MK-headquartered enterprise engineering firm publishing banking case material (e.g. loan-approval automation for a European bank). Case studies are often anonymised but datable, and its LinkedIn/news stream sometimes names partners — useful for supplier-side signals on lending/compliance automation.

source_name: Duna Computers (ULTIMA ERP, fiscal devices) — MK IT vendor
why_relevant: Major MK integrator and fiscal-cash-register manufacturer; relevant to the fiscalisation/e-invoicing (е-Фактура) mandate that intersects bank payment services and merchant acquiring. Corporate/LinkedIn announcements can flag which financial or merchant-acquiring counterparties adopt what.

source_name: Payten / Monri (Asseco payments arm) — news & partner pages
why_relevant: Regional payments vendor (POS deployment, payment gateway, e-commerce) partnered with ~30 banks in the region and part of the Asseco family already active in MK. Its news/partner pages are a likely public trace of POS/gateway/SoftPOS projects at MK private banks, including SCA-driven upgrades.

source_name: eCommerce4all.mk — e-payment processing landscape (MK acquiring/processing map)
why_relevant: Donor/programme-built guide enumerating MK acquiring banks and processors and how online transaction processing is organised; a compact actor map that lets you attribute later vendor announcements to the right bank/processor pair.

source_name: Macedonian Banking Association (MBA) — commissions, incl. AML & regulatory compliance
why_relevant: Sector body whose AML/compliance commission (chaired from Stopanska Banka's compliance division) convenes private banks on incoming mandates; agendas, event pages and named officers point to which compliance topics banks are actively procuring for, and identify the buyer-side people vendors announce deals with.

source_name: e-Nabavki (ESJN) — MK electronic public procurement system, realised contracts grid
why_relevant: Not a source of private-bank RFPs (systemic MK banks are private and out of scope of the Public Procurement Law), but it is the authoritative place to (a) capture the state-owned/state-linked financial entities that DO publish, and (b) build a vendor-name index that can then be matched against private-sector vendor announcements. Explicitly recorded as a negative-coverage boundary for this cell.

source_name: TED / EU procurement platform (as promoted to MK companies)
why_relevant: MK companies are actively pointed to TED (Meta.mk coverage); relevant here mainly for EU-funded projects touching MK payment infrastructure (e.g. the EU-supported MIPS modernisation) where the buyer is public but the implementers are the same vendors that serve private banks. Provides vendor-capability and timeline evidence transferable to the private side.

source_name: Kapital.mk — MK business/finance weekly (fintech and market-infrastructure stories)
why_relevant: Business outlet covering financial-sector technology moves (e.g. Macedonian Stock Exchange tokenisation initiative). Useful for catching vendor-bank or vendor-infrastructure tie-ups that trade press misses, and for identifying new actors to snowball.

source_name: Development Bank of North Macedonia (MBDP) — digitalisation announcements
why_relevant: State development bank that publicly announces digital-product contracts (e.g. digital credit-insurance tool with USAID/Swiss programme support). It is the one bank in MK whose supplier contracting is visible, so it acts as a calibration baseline for what the private banks are doing invisibly, and identifies vendors active in the MK banking market.
